amendments.because: Owner chose to simplify: accept dismisses the remaining findings with the owner's reason instead of adding change-detection rules
amendments.done_when: forge close --resolve accept applies the owner's choice when only the default branch moved or only Forge's own records changed since the stopped review (the check compares the item's own changes against the review's merge base and ignores files under .factory/); --dismiss after a recorded choice works on the same terms; a clean review clears an unanswered review-loop stop; one command test per case; skill.md says so; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

done_when: When the owner records accept at a review-loop stop, forge close records every remaining finding of the latest review as dismissed with the owner's reason and carries on, with no check of whether code or the default branch changed since that review (the owner's choice is the authority); narrow and split stay as they are; a later clean review clears an unanswered stop; one command test per case; skill.md says so; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each
why: The owner's review-loop choice often can't be applied: accept is refused once the default branch moves, a dismissal is refused because recording the choice counts as a change, and a hold stays after a later review comes back clean
